subject: Benchmarking Handoff: throughput/latency matrix and test windows
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@bluehorizon.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Gaurav Singh <gaurav.s@bluehorizon.ai>
Date: 2026-09-12T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Onboarding: perf acceptance criteria / kickoff

Hi Priyom / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Blue Horizon is ready to start the inference onboarding run. To help the internal teams align, here are the high-level acceptance targets we need to validate during the onboarding sprint:

- Steady-state throughput: 650 RPS (90% of requests classified as short prompts, average length 64 tokens)
- Latency SLOs: p50 <= 18 ms, p95 <= 85 ms, cold-start tail p99 <= 250 ms
- Error budget: <= 0.5% 5xx over 24h during load windows
- KV cache effectiveness: reduce token compute by >20% for repeated conversational sessions

We'd like to run two representative load windows next week (one daytime, one overnight) and a longer soak run (4–6 hours) for stability. Can you send a short runbook and point us to the artifacts you expect to collect? Also confirm whether you need client-side simulators from our side or Redwood will drive the RPS generators.

Cheers,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of ML Ops | Blue Horizon AI

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@bluehorizon.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-13T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: perf acceptance criteria / kickoff

Elena — thanks for the clear targets.

Summary / next steps from our side:
- Redwood will run the RPS generators from our dedicated preprod cluster; Blue Horizon can run a client-side generator for cross-validation if you want to mirror your prod traffic.
- Proposed test windows: 2026-09-18 08:00–12:00 PT (day) and 2026-09-19 00:00–04:00 PT (night). Soak run: 2026-09-18 13:00–17:00 PT (4 hours).
- Metrics we will collect: latency distributions (p50/p90/p95/p99), token throughput, GPU utilization, queue depth, 5xx/4xx error counts, KV cache hit ratio, cost-per-1k-tokens estimate.
- Artifacts we'll produce: CSV of raw per-request samples, aggregated KPI matrix (xlsx), system logs tarball, and a one-page preliminary results PDF.

I attached an initial load plan template (bh_onboard_load-plan_v1.csv) and a KPI matrix stub (bh_kpi-matrix.xlsx) — please review and edit the expected request mix column so our simulator matches your traffic.

Can Marissa own coordinating the exact test times with your infra/ops folks? If those windows don't work we can shift. Also copying Ben to ensure we capture profiling traces.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Implementation Lead, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@bluehorizon.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: perf acceptance criteria / kickoff

On Wed, Sep 13, 2026 at 11:22 AM priyom_das@redwood.ai wrote:
> I attached an initial load plan template ... please review and edit the expected request mix

Elena / Gaurav — I'll coordinate with your infra team for the windows. Quick checklist before we start the generators:

1) Traffic template finalized (you or we edit bh_onboard_load-plan_v1.csv) — please confirm by EOD 2026-09-16
2) Test account keys: provide a test API key with the same model/quantization settings we agreed on (scope-limited)
3) Network egress: confirm IP allowlist for our preprod runners (I listed the CIDR block in the attached doc)
4) Logging hooks: enable request id header and forward any internal correlation IDs for tracing

Attached: bh_onboard_load-plan_v1.csv (edit), bh_kpi-matrix.xlsx (measured fields). We'll also collect a simulated client sample if you prefer; otherwise Redwood will run the canonical generator. See note on RPS variance sampling in the CSV.

I'll schedule a 30-minute pre-test sync on 2026-09-17 10:00 PT to finalize keys and allowlists. Please add your infra contact to the invite.

—Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@bluehorizon.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-18T10:48:00-07:00
Subject: Load window 1 — preliminary observations and artifacts

Hi all — quick update from the morning run (2026-09-18 08:00–10:30 PT). We're still aggregating full logs but wanted to share early observations and a short artifact bundle:

- Attached artifacts: rps-sim-logs-20260918.tar.gz, prelim-results-summary.pdf
- Early metrics (sampled): steady-state average RPS: 640 (peak burst 720), p50 latency 16 ms, p95 78 ms, p99 210 ms, 5xx rate 0.12%
- GPU utilization averaged 62% during steady-state; queue depth spiked briefly during the 1-minute synthetic burst but recovered within 20s.
- KV cache hit ratio: measured 26% across repeated sessions (exceeds the >20% target).
- Notes: We observed larger p99 tail during a model reload event around 09:37 PT — traces attached. We're instrumenting a faster warm-start path for the next window.

Link to artifacts and dashboards: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBHZ-onboard-BH-238

Request: Elena — can you confirm whether the burst behavior at ~09:37 matches any spikes on your side (retries/client-side backoff)? Also confirm acceptance criteria: do you want us to re-run the same daytime window after we implement the faster warm-start path, or is the current result acceptable for sign-off?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Systems Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@bluehorizon.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-20T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Load window 1 — preliminary observations and artifacts

Team — thanks for the rapid turnaround and the artifacts. We reviewed the preliminary summary and the Drive dashboards. High level:

- The steady-state numbers look good and meet our contract targets (p50/p95 within thresholds, KV cache >20%).
- The p99 warm-start tail event at 09:37 is acceptable as long as the warm-start mitigation is in place prior to production cutover. Please include the warm-start fix in the rollout notes and provide a 1-hour verification window after it's deployed.
- We request one overnight test (the 2026-09-19 00:00–04:00 PT window) to validate lower-background noise and confirm 5xx stability under longer run conditions.

Action items agreed:
- Redwood: implement warm-start mitigation and schedule a 1-hour verification run (Ben to own)
- Blue Horizon: provide test key and confirm IP allowlist entries by EOD 2026-09-17 (Gaurav) — DONE (we received the key yesterday)
- Marissa / Priyom: wrap up the onboarding runbook and upload final KPI matrix to the Drive folder.

Once we get green on the overnight window we'll sign the onboarding acceptance and schedule production cutover. Appreciate the clear artifacts — prelim-results-summary.pdf is exactly what our procurement team needed for the acceptance packet.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of ML Ops | Blue Horizon AI
